historical_reviews.v3_1: Each visual state needs a distinct, synchronized oracle: steady green with the mapped controller powered and idle, green blinking only during bounded I/O to that controller, and steady amber only while an approved fault state is asserted. The sequence must also prove return to healthy green after the fault is cleared so a latched or neighboring-bay LED is not mistaken for success.

original_test_intent: Validate the physical E1.S bay LED state machine for powered idle, read/write activity and fault, correlated to the correct drive and safe stimuli.
original_method: Map drive serial/controller/BDF to its physical bay and LED, record a powered-idle baseline, run bounded I/O only on an approved test filesystem while an operator captures green blinking, apply one vendor-approved non-destructive fault stimulus while capturing amber and matching telemetry, clear the stimulus, verify healthy recovery, and preserve synchronized video/log evidence.
manual_activity: The storage owner approves the LED map, I/O and fault stimuli; an authorized operator observes and records the exact bay LED while the Agent collects device and BMC evidence.
required_inputs: LED color and blink cadence SPEC
Approved non-system test filesystem and I/O bounds
safety_requirements: Never infer LED state from software inventory
Use only the mapped bay and drive
Do not run I/O on production or raw storage
Bound I/O duration, size and queue depth
Do not create faults by corrupting data, sanitizing, surprise-removing or power-cycling without explicit vendor approval
Stop on media, filesystem, temperature or kernel error
Do not retry an ambiguous fault
agent_execution_scope: Verify drive/bay mapping and storage safety
Collect powered-idle controller and health state
Run only the approved bounded test-file I/O
Timestamp device activity against operator video
Collect read-only fault/BMC/NVMe evidence during approved operator stimulus
Verify post-fault health and archive evidence without judging visual color
engineer_actions: Approve LED pattern tolerances and mapping
Approve designated filesystem and I/O stimulus
Approve and supervise safe fault injection
Direct storage recovery on any error
Decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED for each bay

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `nvme list` only enumerate devices; they do not drive read/write activity, assert a defined fault or observe solid/blinking green or amber. The unsafe SSH method also compromises provenance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only inventory/health collection, one approved bounded regular-file I/O workload for activity, and only the vendor-approved fault tool or operator procedure; synchronize all telemetry with visual capture of the mapped LED.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All three visual states and the 20-minute source duration remain; stimulus details and tolerances require owner approval.

modernized_recommendation.status: DRIVE-CORRELATED THREE-STATE LED STIMULUS AND RECOVERY TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prove bay identity first, then capture idle green, I/O-correlated green cadence, approved-fault amber and recovered healthy state in one timestamped controller/LED timeline.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe, bounded stimuli, software corroboration, cadence tolerance and recovery while preserving the physical visual criteria.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Enumeration proves neither LED wiring nor color/pattern behavior; even visible blinking can belong to another drive unless activity is isolated and correlated to its controller.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Fault injection and writes can affect media or data, and color/cadence remain physical observations that the Agent cannot independently certify.

SUT/backplane/firmware identity, test-volume proof, operator/camera and timestamps

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require the same three E1.S LED states. The fault mechanism is unspecified but is a prerequisite rather than contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The LED state-machine purpose is clear and a vendor-approved safe fault method can be requested. Execution is gated by that package/operator input, so the case is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Replaces an unrelated inventory-only result with drive-specific visual stimuli, safe fault boundaries and a recovery checkpoint that actually test the LED state machine.
independent_technical_reasoning: LED validation is a causal correlation problem: the mapped controller must enter a known state at the same time the correct physical indicator changes. A solid amber photograph without a defined fault proves only that a lamp was lit, and activity blinking during general system I/O may belong to another bay. Isolated stimuli, synchronized telemetry and restoration to a healthy state are needed to close both identity and state transitions.
